task: E — bilingual search, localization and browser speech services
testsRun: npm test -- tests/unit/search.test.ts tests/unit/i18n.test.ts tests/unit/audio.test.ts: PASS, 36 tests
assumptions: Unsupported language values fall back to English; Arabic regional tags resolve to Arabic.
Search preserves original Room objects and inventory order for equal relevance; caller selects the public inventory.
Search-only normalization maps ta marbuta to ha, Arabic/Persian digits to ASCII, and Arabic/Persian ya/kaf variants to common forms.
Numeric terms never use fuzzy correction, although code-prefix search is supported.
Browser speech API availability does not assert that an Arabic or English voice is installed. Matching voices are used only if the browser reports them.
handoffNotes: Search exports normalizeSearch(text) and searchRooms(rooms, query, language='en'). Arabic and English names and aliases are always searchable.
i18n exports dictionary, dictionaries (alias), TranslationKey, getDirection, resolveLanguage and t. Unknown translation keys return the key; all dictionary entries have both languages.

Dictionary keys cover search, map controls, room details, route states, calibration/accessibility notices, audio, language, keyboard navigation, categories and loading/error states. Inspect TranslationKey or dictionary.en for the exact list.

createBrowserTTS returns the four-method TTSService. Create once, call speak(currentDescription, activeLanguage) for playback or replay, stop on selection/language changes and cleanup, and setMuted for mute state. No direct browser speech dependency is needed in UI.
Speech API access is lazy for SSR; each new utterance cancels the previous one. Unmuting never triggers playback automatically. Browser failures are contained.
